description: Software incident response: severity, on-call, escalation, communication and postmortems.

units.title: Incident severity levels
units.text:
| Severity | Criteria | First response |
|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Full outage or data loss affecting customers | Page on-call immediately; incident commander assigned within 15 minutes |
| SEV2 | Major feature degraded for many users | Page on-call; acknowledge within 30 minutes |
| SEV3 | Minor defect with a workaround | Ticket for the next business day |

units.title: Incident commander
units.text: The person who coordinates the response to a major incident: assigns roles, decides on mitigations and owns communication. While holding the role they do not debug the system themselves.

units.title: Escalation
units.text: If the primary on-call engineer does not acknowledge a page within 10 minutes, it escalates to the secondary on-call. After another 10 minutes without acknowledgement it goes to the engineering manager.

units.title: Postmortems
units.text: Every SEV1 and SEV2 incident gets a written postmortem within five business days. Postmortems are blameless: they describe what the system allowed to happen, not who made a mistake.

units.title: Blameless reviews surface more causes
units.text: When people are not afraid of punishment they report in detail what they did and saw, which reveals contributing factors that a blame-focused review would hide.

units.title: Customer communication
units.text: For a SEV1 the status page is updated within 20 minutes of declaring the incident and then at least every hour until it is resolved. SEV3 incidents are not posted on the status page.

units.title: On-call rotation
units.text: Each engineer is on call for one week out of every six. The handover takes place on Mondays at 10:00 and includes a short review of open alerts.

units.title: Roll back before you debug
units.text: When a deploy is suspected of causing an incident, the first mitigation is to return to the previous version. The investigation of the root cause continues afterwards, once customers are no longer affected.

units.title: Change freeze
units.text: While a SEV1 is active, all non-emergency deploys are frozen. Only changes approved by the incident commander may be released.

units.title: Runbook
units.text: A step-by-step guide attached to a known alert that tells the on-call engineer how to diagnose and mitigate it without needing to understand the whole system.

units.title: Reliability metrics
units.text:
| Metric | Target | Last quarter |
|---|---|---|
| Mean time to acknowledge | 5 min | 7 min |
| Mean time to resolve a SEV1 | 2 h | 3.5 h |
| Postmortems delivered on time | 100% | 92% |

units.title: On-call compensation
units.text: Engineers receive a fixed stipend for each on-call week, plus an extra day off after any night in which they were paged for more than two hours.

units.title: Security incidents
units.text: Suspected security breaches are handled by the security team, not by the regular on-call rotation. The on-call engineer only preserves the logs and notifies security.

units.title: Changing severity
units.text: The incident commander may lower the severity once customer impact is mitigated, but the postmortem requirement follows the highest severity the incident reached.
